name: quant-protocol-v1
status: frozen before any calendar, cycle or event scan was run on market data
principle: universal pattern search manufactures coincidences; every test is registered in a family, corrected, confirmed on chronologically later data, and only prospective observations can give final predictive evidence

data.btc_spot: Binance spot BTCUSDT 1h and 1d official archives (checksummed), from 2017-08-17; perpetual-futures data of earlier missions is not used here

fred.DGS10: 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield, daily (public domain, US Treasury via FRED)
fred.SP500: S&P 500 daily close (FRED, S&P Dow Jones Indices licence: research use, ~10 years available)
fred.DFEDTARU: fed funds target range upper limit (from 2008-12-16)

unavailable.CPI / NFP release calendar: bls.gov returns HTTP 403 from this environment
unavailable.consensus expectations / surprises: require licensed survey data (not available); 'above expectations' interactions cannot be tested
unavailable.intraday S&P / Nasdaq / gold: not available; equity analysis is daily and limited to ~10 years

time_conventions.btc_daily_return: close-to-close of Binance daily candles, day = UTC date of the candle open (00:00 UTC)
time_conventions.fomc_event_time: scheduled statement release 14:00 America/New_York on the final meeting day, converted to UTC with DST
time_conventions.election_day: statutory U.S. federal election day: Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even years (2 U.S.C. 7); market reaction measured from the close of election day

periods.exposure_note: CONFIRMATION is chronologically held out from every quant scan, but BTC prices of that period were seen in other project contexts (strategy validation, forecasting backtests); it is therefore not independent of the operator's exposure. Only PROSPECTIVE is independent.

F-DOM.named_hypothesis: H-DOM-14: the 14th differs from other days on any metric

F-TOM.what: turn of month (last day + first 3 days)

F-CYCLE.what: periodogram ordinate at 7, 30.44, 91.31, 365.25 days for daily returns and |returns| vs the local band [P/2, 2P]

F-XEVENT.what: FOMC x pre-event 30-day volatility regime; FOMC x policy action (target change vs hold, DFEDTARU)

F-ELECT.inference: only if n >= 20 events; otherwise descriptive with placebo percentiles and an explicit sample-size warning

F-FCAST.what: forecast feature fomc_in_window (scheduled statement inside (o, o+h]; calendars are published in advance, so the feature is point-in-time)
F-FCAST.comparison: M1_logistic + feature vs M1_logistic on rv_24, move3_24, move5_24, forecast protocol v1 machinery, SCREEN period, block bootstrap, Holm over 3
F-FCAST.promotion: never automatic; at most a prospective challenger

methods.calendar: rotation test: the calendar labels are compared with returns circularly shifted by a random offset (999 shifts, seed 0), which keeps volatility clustering and dependence intact; two-sided p = (1 + #|null| >= |obs|) / 1000
methods.event_study: placebo resampling: event mean vs 2000 means of equally many placebo times drawn from the same period at the same weekday and clock time (non-event days); bootstrap CI over events (2000, seed 0); effects reported as event minus placebo median
methods.cycle: rank of the periodogram ordinate at P within ordinates in [P/2, 2P]; also reported separately in each half of the period
methods.multiple_testing: per family: Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.10 on DISCOVERY (exploratory survivors); survivors re-tested once on CONFIRMATION, one-sided in the discovery direction, Holm at alpha 0.05 across that family's survivors

status_rules.supported: survives BH on discovery AND Holm on confirmation in the same direction (still exploratory until prospective evidence)
status_rules.inconclusive: survives discovery but not confirmation, or confirmation n < 20
status_rules.rejected: does not survive BH on discovery

validation_of_the_method: tests must show that synthetic i.i.d. data rarely produce a 'supported' calendar finding and that a planted effect of adequate size is recovered

budget.network: official archives and public pages only, cached with checksums

amendment_1.after: after development dry runs of F-DOM/F-DOW/F-MOY/F-TOM/F-FOMC/F-ELECT/F-CYCLE (deterministic; the registered run reproduces them) and BEFORE any forecast-feature result was computed
changes: F-FCAST additionally tests 'saturday_target_day' (the 24 h target window is a Saturday, UTC) for rv_24, move3_24, move5_24, because F-DOW:5 (Saturday |return| and left-tail rate) reached 'supported'. The F-FCAST Holm family therefore has 6 tests instead of 3. The feature was chosen BECAUSE of the calendar result: its forecast test is a pipeline step, not independent confirmation of the calendar finding.

F-ELECT reference point corrected before reporting: the last observation at or before election day (bond markets were closed on many election days; the first implementation silently dropped those events).

amendment_2.trigger: the method-validation test required by this protocol (planted day-14 effect, ~5 standard errors) was recovered 0/10 times
amendment_2.diagnosis: an empirical rotation p-value has resolution 1/(N+1) = 0.001 with 999 rotations; BH's first threshold in F-DOM is 0.10/124 = 0.0008, so a single day-of-month effect could never be detected (the method was powerless by construction for isolated effects)
amendment_2.change: calendar p-values use the rotation null's mean and standard deviation (dependence-preserving) with a two-sided normal approximation: p = erfc(|obs - mean_null| / (sd_null * sqrt 2)); one-sided analogues for confirmation. The empirical rotation p is still reported. All other rules unchanged.
amendment_2.disclosure: this amendment was written after development dry runs whose real-data results had been seen (14th: rejected; Saturday |return|: supported). The change was forced by the synthetic validation, not chosen to alter a real-data conclusion; the registered run below supersedes the dry runs, whatever it shows. The false-anomaly test is re-run under the new p-values.

amendment_3.trigger: P4: CPI and Employment Situation release dates became available from ALFRED vintages (bls.gov is blocked); written BEFORE any BTC data around these releases was examined in this project

F-MACRO.events: category macro_release, kind first_release, subcategories cpi and nfp (ALFRED vintage dates 2017-08..2026-10; 08:30 ET by agency convention)
F-MACRO.window_start: the hourly bar containing the release (opens 08:00 ET, i.e. 30 min BEFORE the release; hourly bars cannot start at 08:30)
F-MACRO.placebo: 08:00 ET bars on non-release days with the same weekday set as the subcategory's releases, excluding +-1 day around any macro release (cpi, nfp, gdp) and +-2 days around FOMC meetings; matched placebo resampling as F-FOMC (2000 draws, +1 correction)
F-MACRO.decision: BH q=0.10 over the 8 DISCOVERY tests; survivors get ONE one-sided matched-placebo test on CONFIRMATION, Holm alpha=0.05, same sign, n_confirmation >= 20 -> supported (exploratory)
F-MACRO.forecast_integration: only if a primary metric is supported: feature 'macro_release_in_window' tested as M1 + feature vs M1 on the forecast SCREEN period with the existing F-FCAST procedure; never promoted without prospective evidence
F-MACRO.not_testable: surprise / above-expectations effects (no consensus data); GDP (quarterly, n < 20 per period)

amendment_3.disclosure: general market lore says CPI/NFP days are volatile for risk assets; this is a prior belief, not an observation from this project's data. Confirmation-period BTC prices were seen in other project contexts (see periods.exposure_note).
amendment_3.unchanged: all thresholds, periods and existing families

amendment_4.trigger: quant_calibration_v1 showed F-DOW producing ~8x its expected share of false 'supported' results (13/300 under iid); diagnosis: circular rotations with the same shift mod 7 give near-identical weekday statistics, so the F-DOW rotation null has only ~6 clusters (essentially the other weekdays) and the amendment-2 normal approximation is invalid for this family (an exact rank p of ~1/7 became z = -2.7 for Saturday |return|)
amendment_4.change: F-DOW only: within-week label permutation. Restrict the period to complete Monday-Sunday weeks; effect of weekday d = mean over d minus mean over the other six days of the same weeks; null = 4999 joint random permutations of the 7 values inside every week (preserves all between-week volatility dependence); two-sided empirical p = (1 + #{|null - mean_null| >= |obs - mean_null|}) / 5000; one-sided analogues for confirmation. Decision rule unchanged (BH 0.10 on DISCOVERY, one-sided Holm 0.05 on CONFIRMATION, same sign, n >= 20).
amendment_4.acceptance_before_real_data: the corrected F-DOW rule must first pass synthetic calibration with the quant_calibration_v1 generators and seeds (300 per generator, F-DOW only): per-family false-supported Wilson 95% upper bound <= 3% under every generator. If it fails, F-DOW is reported as 'no valid method' and no F-DOW status is used anywhere.
amendment_4.supersedes: all F-DOW statuses from the rotation method (registered runs c20261103T2323577382, c20261103T233607736b) once the corrected run is registered; those rows stay in the registry, marked superseded
amendment_4.disclosure: written after the rotation-based F-DOW results had been seen (Saturday |return| and left-tail: supported). The change is forced by the synthetic calibration, not chosen for a real-data outcome; whatever the corrected run shows supersedes, including a loss of support.
amendment_4.unchanged: F-DOM, F-MOY, F-TOM (their per-family calibration rates were within expectation), periods, thresholds

amendment_5.trigger: amendment 4 re-run made F-DOW:6:mean_absret (Sunday lower) and F-DOW:0:mean_absret (Monday higher) 'supported'; by the existing F-FCAST pipeline rule (as for Saturday) each supported weekday becomes a candidate forecast feature

F-FCAST-2.method: identical to F-FCAST (M1 + feature vs M1, forecast protocol v1 rolling origin, block bootstrap on SCREEN; DEV mean must not be worse); Holm 0.05 over these 6 only
F-FCAST-2.outcome: passing features become prospective challengers CH:<feature> (never replacing the champion), governed by challenger_policy_v1; Saturday tests are not re-run

amendment_5.disclosure: the forecast SCREEN and DEV periods are previously exposed; this is selection evidence only. The weekday effects themselves were found on the same daily data; the feature test is a pipeline step, not independent confirmation.

amendment_6.trigger: quant_calibration_v2: per-family false-supported Wilson upper bounds 3.4-3.8% for F-DOM and F-MOY exceed the 3% bound pre-stated in agenda A3 (decision D-99c58ca842)
amendment_6.change: Replace the rotation null by within-block label permutation: F-DOM and F-TOM permute day labels within each calendar month (preserves month-level volatility); F-MOY permutes month labels among the calendar months of each year (preserves year-level volatility). Weekday adjustment, metrics, effects (in-label minus out-of-label mean), periods and the decision rule (BH 0.10 discovery, one-sided Holm 0.05 confirmation, same sign, n >= 20) are unchanged. 4999 permutations, empirical p as amendment 4.
amendment_6.acceptance_before_real_data: with the quant_calibration_v2 generators and seeds (300 per generator), each of F-DOM, F-MOY, F-TOM must have a per-family false-supported Wilson 95% upper bound <= 3% under every generator; planted day-14 mean-shift power is reported (no threshold). If a family fails, it is reported as 'no valid method' and no status of that family is used.
amendment_6.supersedes: F-DOM, F-MOY and F-TOM statuses of the rotation-method runs once the corrected run is registered (rows kept)
amendment_6.disclosure: written after all rotation-method F-DOM/F-MOY/F-TOM results were seen (all rejected, including the 14th). The change is forced by calibration; the corrected run supersedes whatever it shows, including new discoveries, which would then need confirmation like any other.

amendment_7.trigger: director agenda: cross-asset information (priority 3); equity-market volatility and moves are a plausible driver of BTC volatility (risk appetite, shared investors)

features.vix_log_lag: log(VIXCLS) of the latest FRED observation dated <= origin_date - 3 days
features.spx_absret_lag: |log change| of FRED SP500 between its two latest observations dated <= origin_date - 3 days

F-FCAST-3.point_in_time: origin O is 00:00 UTC, information cutoff as_of = O - 24 h; observations dated <= O - 3 days closed >= 27 h before as_of and are on FRED before issuance (which happens after the BTC archive of O-1... i.e. on day O-1); no observation after the cutoff can enter
F-FCAST-3.method: identical to F-FCAST (M1 + feature vs M1, forecast protocol v1 rolling origin, block bootstrap on SCREEN; DEV mean not worse); Holm 0.05 over these 6
F-FCAST-3.outcome: passing features become prospective challengers only after (a) the scheduler fetches FRED daily and (b) their own power analysis is computed before outcomes (challenger_policy_v2: they do NOT join the efficacy family without a new policy version)

amendment_7.disclosure: BTC SCREEN/DEV periods are previously exposed; VIX/SP500 have not been used as BTC forecast features in this project before. General market knowledge that VIX and crypto volatility co-move is a prior, not a result from this project.

amendment_8.trigger: director agenda (priority 3: microstructure and derivatives): Binance's official archive publishes BTCUSDT futures metrics (5-min open interest, taker long/short volume ratio) and 1h premium-index klines on the same daily cadence as the price archive

features.oi_logchg_7d: log(open interest at the last 5-min row before as_of) - log(open interest at the last row before as_of - 7 days)  [leverage build-up -> liquidation-driven volatility]
features.taker_logratio_24h: mean of log(taker long/short volume ratio) over the 5-min rows in [as_of - 24 h, as_of)  [one-sided aggressive flow]
features.premium_abs_24h: mean |premium index close| over the 1h premium-index bars that closed by as_of in the last 24 h  [perp crowding vs index]

F-FCAST-4.point_in_time: only rows timestamped strictly before the forecast information cutoff as_of (= origin - 24 h) are used; these files are published on the same D+1 cadence as the price archive used for as_of
F-FCAST-4.method: identical to F-FCAST (M1 + feature vs M1, forecast protocol v1 rolling origin, block bootstrap on SCREEN; DEV mean not worse); Holm 0.05 over these 9
F-FCAST-4.outcome: passing features are candidates only; activation as prospective challengers requires a journaled decision, daily ingestion of these files by the scheduler, and a power analysis before outcomes (challenger_policy_v2)

amendment_8.disclosure: written before these derivatives files were downloaded or examined in this project; BTC SCREEN/DEV periods are previously exposed; the simulator's cascade research (v0.5) motivates the open-interest hypothesis (prior, not a result on these data)
